asked: a second red make done in a row
why: The four red gates each failed on a different real fault, and each was cleared by the commit after it: test-full at 901257c16, static at 30f685711, then seeds twice. The two seeds reds are 30 seconds apart with only a run-log file between them. That was a rerun of unchanged code, which the no-fixed-seeds check rightly failed again, since it keeps testing a failing seed until it passes. The wasted run cost about 100 s, well under the 10-minute bar, so there is no tooling fix. The bundle shows no oscillation and no packing (a symmetry defect in the dry plot lap test, with no unresearched number being defended), so the gate found a real defect and the loop is not at fault. The session reports the fix (8ffb84a2a, with a unit test that is red without it, comb seed 549270514 rolling clean, and 600 fresh seeds passing), but the bundle does not show it, so the next gate must prove it.
what: The next round is one make done at or after 8ffb84a2a. It must be green on every phase, seeds included: the no-fixed-seeds check with seed 549270514 rolled again, plus the dry_on_dry unit test that is red without the fix. No other round is owed. If seeds goes red again on a different seed, that is a new defect to fix the same way. If it goes red on 549270514 again, the fix did not hold: revert or fix it before any rerun, and never rerun the gate on unchanged code.

asked: Feature 449, phase 1. T027's plan review BLOCKED decision (b): the ledger guard runs ledger_lint.py, ledger_owed.py and review_cost.py by path until phase 3. The review reads FR-001's "the libraries its guards call - phase 1" as covering any Python a guard runs by path. Earlier reviews of the same shape went the other way: T006 (a), which named `scripts/reviews/checkpoint.py`, `review_owed.py` and `review_prereq.py`, was CLEAR; T018's decision (b) and T024's decision (b), ruled LEGITIMATE on FR-001's phase 2 wording; T025's review of a phase-3 tool (speckit-todo.py) was NOT LEGITIMATE. Question: for a phase-1 guard that consults by path a Python file FR-001 assigns by name to phase 2 or 3, is "asked by path until its own phase" within phase 1, or must the tool be ported with the guard (what the T027 review says)? The answer sets the shape of ~25 remaining guard tasks and the phase's cost.
why: Asked by path until its own phase is within phase 1. Six tasks' reviews cleared this shape (T006 (a) on the same scripts/reviews/ residual clause, T008, T012, T013, T018, T024) and T027 (b) alone blocked it, saying T006 and T024 were not in its bundle and that each decision is ruled on its own; porting these tools now would also put phase 3 ahead of phase 2 against FR-001's order, and Story 3 names the review tooling under scripts/ as phase 3, a line T027's review did not weigh. This is sequencing rather than what to build: both routes end at SC-005's empty census, as T027's review concedes, and the T025 NOT LEGITIMATE the question cites is not in the evidence (T025's recorded decisions are all within or LEGITIMATE), so it carries no weight here.
what: 1. Amend FR-001's phase-1 clause by one sentence, the amendment T027's review asked for, since reviewers rule on the spec text and a cited precedent does not bind them: the libraries its guards call are the code under scripts/hooks/ and any module only guards use; a Python file elsewhere that has callers of its own (gate, push, a make target) stays in its own phase and a guard may run it by path until then. Take it through spec-fidelity once. 2. The line for T027 and every remaining guard task, each block stating it: everything under scripts/hooks/ is phase 1 with no deferral (check T006's and T012's hm_arbiter.py and hm_dropped.py against this; if they live there, T052's census owes them); a file whose only caller is the guard is ported with the guard, as T026 did hm_budget.py; the guard's own deciding is Rust; the by-path ask is on a rare branch only, never on the plain Bash or Edit path SC-001 measures, and last where the verdict allows, as T018 (b2); a small read that is really the guard's own logic moves in-process, as T025 (b). 3. T027 (b) stands as planned: rewrite the block to quote and answer the phase-1 clause, and to say how the decider's unit tests reach the git commit branch under FR-008 without starting Python (the tool's path stubbed in the unit test, the real tool in the suite replay), then re-review it. 4. T052's phase-1 record lists every by-path Python ask left and the phase that removes it. No packing in this bundle.

asked: T038 (wakeup guard) has one suite case: stdin that is not JSON is refused. The shell knew the tool only from its settings matcher. Round 1 ruled NOT LEGITIMATE a list reached only by the --only replay. Round 2 ruled NOT LEGITIMATE giving the layer its own settings entry, because FR-007 says one process for a tool call and that adds a second process on a ScheduleWakeup call. The third route, a general entry with a negative-lookahead matcher so ScheduleWakeup has only its own entry, would put every guard of every tool on an untested harness regex behavior: if the harness rejected it, all Rust guards would silently stop. Measured: 73,328 guard-log rows hold one wakeup unreadable refusal, 2026-09-26 (the day the guard was written), with empty session, cwd and tool, so no real tool call. Which should it be: keep the second entry (one extra process on a tool only /loop uses, refusal kept on the real path), or change the suite case's expected verdict so non-JSON is nothing to judge, as every other guard already reads it? (REVIEW=plan: an accept stands as the plan review's verdict)
why: Change the case's expected verdict: the second entry spends a real process on every real ScheduleWakeup call against FR-007's bare MUST, and bends production through --only and CLOSED_ON_GARBAGE to keep one verdict on an input no real call has been recorded sending, while the verdict change alters nothing on any real call and matches what every other guard reads (T012). FR-002's exception does not literally cover this, because non-JSON stdin is not correct work, so this ruling is the waiver for this one case; it rests on the guard log's single unreadable refusal, with empty session, cwd and tool, on the day the guard was written (the 73,328 rows are all guards' rows, so the weight is in that the one row is no tool call and that the harness speaks one protocol to every guard, not in the size of the denominator). The ruling is continue rather than accept because an accept would stand as the plan review's verdict on the plan as it reads now, and its T038 (b) still holds the second entry round 2 ruled NOT LEGITIMATE.
what: Route B, and only it. (1) Rewrite T038 decision (b) in plan.md: no ScheduleWakeup settings entry of its own, no CLOSED_ON_GARBAGE list and no --only branch for it; the PreToolUse layer runs in the one whole-binary process for a ScheduleWakeup call, so FR-007 holds. The negative-lookahead matcher is rejected too. (2) The suite case for stdin that is not JSON keeps its input and its expected verdict becomes nothing to judge, as T012 reads it for every other guard; the change is named in the commit and in phase 1's record as FR-002 requires, citing this ruling. (3) Add one clause to FR-002 naming this case and citing the round arbiter's ruling of 2026-11-08, ask:449-T038-garbage, in the form FR-001 already cites ask:449-phase1-tools-by-path, so SC-004 and later drift checks read true. (4) Decision (a) is untouched: the refusal on an unreadable transcript at the call, open at the turn end, keeps its cases and verdicts; a real call the guard cannot read through its transcript still refuses. (5) The plan review's next round reads the rewritten block for whether it says this and nothing more; the waiver itself is settled here and is not reopened in that round.

asked: T029 decision (c), the XIV fix that a scratch file whose text names a guard is not a guard write, has had three plan-review rounds, each NOT LEGITIMATE on the exemption's reach. Round 1: piped or stored-and-run bodies. Round 2: a chained opener line and a run through a glob. Round 3: an unquoted delimiter, whose body the shell runs. Each was a real gap and each is now fixed; round 3 said only one clause was wrong and named the change, which is applied word for word: the exemption is a whole call that is one storing cat or tee, a quoted delimiter, nothing else. New refused-direction cases pin every form. Should this block's changed clause take a fourth review round, or does your accept stand as the review's verdict? The bundle's guard did not count these per-task rounds, so round 3 ran without a ruling first. (REVIEW=plan: an accept stands as the plan review's verdict)
why: The three per-task rounds (spec-fidelity, 16:19, 16:23 and 16:29 in the cascade) each found a new gap, none repeated or reversed, and the exemption has narrowed to a closed form, so the loop is converging and is not a process fault; their findings are not in the bundle, so that history is the session's account. The clause as it reads still has a material gap no round named, and an accept would make it the plan review's verdict: 'its one redirect' does not restrict the target, and measured 2026-11-08 under a quoted delimiter, `cat > >(bash) <<'EOF'` and `tee >(bash) >/dev/null <<'EOF'` both executed the body, which falsifies the clause's 'no command in the call can run what was stored'. This is not packing (tooling, no researched value moves), and the uncounted round 3 cost one short dispatch that found a real gap, so no tooling fix clears the bar.
what: One fourth round, on T029 (c)'s changed clause only. First amend the clause: the storing target (cat's one redirect, every tee file argument) must be a word of plain path characters and $NAME expansions, with no process substitution, command substitution or backquote anywhere on the opener line; `$S/...` must stay allowed, because the logged case the fix exists for uses it. Name tee's file arguments, which the clause's 'its one redirect' does not describe. Add refused-direction cases for `cat > >(bash) <<'EOF'` and `tee >(bash) <<'EOF'` to test-make-only-hooks.sh. The round looks at that amendment and at whether the closed form now makes the clause's 'no command can run what was stored' true; it does not reopen forms already refused. In the implementation, pin the terminator as bash reads it: with `<<-'EOF'` a tab-indented EOF ends the body (measured), so what follows it is 'after the terminator' and must not be blanked. If the round is clear, the block stands and T029 goes on; any further NOT LEGITIMATE on this clause comes back as a new ask, not a fifth round.

asked: ask:449-T029-stored allowed one fourth round on T029 (c) and said any further NOT LEGITIMATE on this clause comes back as a new ask. Round 4 ruled the storing-target clause LEGITIMATE and found one more gap: a NAME=value before the cat can be PATH=<dir>, which changes what cat runs (measured by the reviewer on bash 5.3.9). The reviewer named the change, no assignment may name PATH or a loader variable. Applied wider than asked: an assignment's name must be one letter or lowercase, so it cannot be PATH, LD_*, BASH_ENV, IFS or any other name the shell or a loader reads; the logged case's S= is one letter. Refused-direction cases pin PATH and LD_PRELOAD. Four rounds have each narrowed the same exemption and the code already refuses every named form. Accept this as the review's verdict, or say what remains. (REVIEW=plan: an accept stands as the plan review's verdict)
why: Round 4's finding (a PATH= assignment changing what cat runs) was new and is already in clause (c) as it reads now, and the session's fix is stricter than the reviewer asked: an assignment's name must be one letter or lowercase. A change that only shrinks the exemption can refuse more but cannot open the kind of gap these rounds were finding, so a fifth round to confirm it buys little; nothing reverses, the event log shows no oscillation and the fixes did not re-owe more checks, so this is a review working through a hand-written exemption, not a faulty loop. Limits of this ruling: the bundle holds the plan text and not the Rust or the suite, and does not show T029's own review blocks, so the claims that the code refuses every named form and that round 4 ruled the storing-target clause LEGITIMATE are the session's report, unchecked here.
what: T029 (c) stands as the plan review's verdict as plan.md reads now; no fifth round on this clause. The session implements against it and goes on: make_only_hooks must hold the one-letter-or-lowercase rule and test-make-only-hooks.sh must pin both directions, including the refused PATH and LD_PRELOAD cases named in the question and the forms the clause lists, with the verdict change from refused to pass named for that one form alone in the commit and in phase 1's record (FR-002). Any further form found during implementation is a new suite case and a commit note under FR-002, not a plan round. Nothing is left open on the clause.
